questions.question: 🦅 Sami examines a patient with a 6 mm pocket. He says: 'Root planing and that's it!' 🐆 Mina replies: 'And the re-evaluation?' Why is re-evaluation crucial?
options: It allows assessment of the response to treatment and adjustment of the care plan
It is useless because treatment is always effective
It is reserved only for complex cases
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Re-evaluation at 4-6 weeks is essential to measure pocket reduction and decide on the next steps.' 🦅 Sami: 'Fine, OK, but it's long...'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing an 8 mm pocket with bone loss, proposes: 'Periodontal flap.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'No, laser!' What is the indication for the flap?
options: Deep pockets > 5 mm with accessible bone loss
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'The flap is indicated for access and debridement of deep pockets with bone loss.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you know your indications!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing aggressive periodontitis in a 25-year-old patient, says: 'It's genetic, we can't do anything.' 🐆 Mina replies: 'Yes, we can treat it!' What is aggressive periodontitis?
options: A rapid form of periodontitis in young and healthy patients
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Aggressive periodontitis occurs in young patients without local risk factors.' 🦅 Sami: 'I didn't know it could be treated effectively.'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing a patient with aggressive periodontitis, says: 'We need associated antibiotic therapy.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'No, scaling is enough.' What is the validated strategy?
options: Amoxicillin + metronidazole in combination with scaling
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'The amoxicillin-metronidazole combination is recommended in aggressive periodontitis.' 🦅 Sami: 'I prefer to avoid antibiotics, but you're right.'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a Miller Class II recession, says: 'We can cover it 100%.' 🐆 Mina replies: 'The prognosis is guarded.' What is the Miller classification?
options: Class I and II: complete coverage possible, Class III: partial, Class IV: impossible
Only classes I and II exist
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Miller classifies recessions according to the coverage prognosis.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you're unbeatable today!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing a Grade 3 furcation, says: 'The prognosis is guarded.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'We can always treat it!' What is a Grade 3 furcation?
options: A through-and-through furcation involvement with communication between roots
An involvement of less than 2 mm
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'A Grade 3 furcation is through-and-through, complicating hygiene and treatment.' 🦅 Sami: 'I'll try to treat it anyway...'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a patient with a 5 mm pocket after treatment, says: 'The treatment has failed.' 🐆 Mina replies: 'Not necessarily!' What does the literature say?
options: A residual 5 mm pocket can be stable with good plaque control
Any pocket > 4 mm is a failure
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'A residual pocket can be maintained stable with good plaque control.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you're right this time!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing a patient with severe periodontitis, says: 'We need a complete assessment.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'Useless, the diagnosis is obvious.' What does the complete assessment include?
options: Complete probing, X-rays, plaque, bleeding, and mobility indices
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'The complete assessment evaluates severity, extent, and prognosis.' 🦅 Sami: 'Fine, we'll do everything... but it's long!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing vertical bone loss, says: 'It's lost, we need to extract.' 🐆 Mina replies: 'We can regenerate!' What is guided tissue regeneration?
options: A technique using membranes and biomaterials to regenerate bone
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'GTR allows regeneration of bone lost around teeth.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you're really up to date!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing Grade 3 mobility, says: 'The prognosis is very guarded.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'We can still treat!' What does Grade 3 mobility mean?
options: Horizontal mobility > 2 mm or vertical mobility
Horizontal mobility of less than 1 mm
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Grade 3 mobility is severe, with a very guarded prognosis.' 🦅 Sami: 'I'll try to save it anyway...'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a patient with a 7 mm pocket and bleeding, says: 'It's active periodontitis.' 🐆 Mina asks: 'How to confirm it?' What is bleeding on probing?
options: A sign of active inflammation and disease progression
A sign of poor hygiene only
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'BOP is an indicator of inflammatory activity.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you're making progress!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing a patient with periodontitis and uncontrolled diabetes, says: 'We need to control diabetes first.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'No, we treat periodontitis first.' Who is right?
options: Mina, diabetes control improves the response to periodontal treatment
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'The relationship is bidirectional, but controlled diabetes optimizes results.' 🦅 Sami: 'Fine, we'll coordinate with his doctor...'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a patient with periodontitis and active smoking, says: 'Tobacco has no impact on treatment.' 🐆 Mina replies: 'Yes, absolutely!' What is the impact of tobacco?
options: It reduces vascularization and the response to periodontal treatment
It improves the response to treatment
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Tobacco compromises vascularization and healing.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you're on fire today!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing a patient with periodontitis, says: 'We need X-rays.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'Useless, I can see the pockets.' What type of X-ray is indicated?
options: Periapical X-rays to evaluate bone loss
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Periapicals show bone loss precisely.' 🦅 Sami: 'Fine, we'll do them...'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a Grade 2 furcation lesion, says: 'We can treat it with filling.' 🐆 Mina replies: 'The prognosis is guarded.' What is a Grade 2 furcation?
options: A partial furcation involvement, visible but not through-and-through
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Grade 2 furcation is partial, accessible but difficult to treat.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you know your classification!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing a patient with a periodontal abscess, says: 'We need to drain immediately.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'No, antibiotics are enough.' Who is right?
options: Mina, drainage is urgent to evacuate the pus
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Drainage is the first emergency, then antibiotics.' 🦅 Sami: 'OK, I'll drain... but quickly!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a patient with a 6 mm pocket after surgery, says: 'The surgery has failed.' 🐆 Mina replies: 'Not necessarily!' What does the literature say?
options: A stable 5-6 mm pocket can be acceptable if non-inflammatory
Any pocket > 4 mm is a failure
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'A stable residual pocket can be maintained with good control.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you're being reasonable!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing severe generalized periodontitis, says: 'We need global treatment.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'No, by quadrant.' Which approach is recommended?
options: Treatment by quadrant in several sessions is validated
Global treatment in a single session
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Treatment by quadrant is the standard strategy to minimize discomfort.' 🦅 Sami: 'I prefer to do everything at once, but you're right.'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a Miller Class III recession, says: 'We can graft successfully.' 🐆 Mina replies: 'Coverage will be incomplete.' What is the prognosis?
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Miller III has partial coverage, but improvement is possible.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you're really an expert!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing a patient with severe periodontitis and a family history, says: 'There is a genetic component.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'Genetics is not important.' What is the role of genetics?
options: Genetics influences susceptibility and immune response
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Certain genetic variants increase susceptibility to periodontitis.' 🦅 Sami: 'I didn't know, thank you Mina!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a patient with a 4 mm pocket after maintenance, says: 'It's a relapse.' 🐆 Mina replies: 'Not necessarily!' What does a 4 mm pocket mean?
options: A 4 mm pocket can be stable if non-inflammatory
Any 4 mm pocket is a relapse
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'A stable 4 mm pocket with negative BOP is acceptable.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you're becoming cautious!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing general bone loss, says: 'We need a prosthetic evaluation.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'No, we treat periodontitis first.' What is the sequence?
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Periodontal treatment must stabilize the periodontium before prosthetics.' 🦅 Sami: 'I agree with you!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a patient with periodontitis, says: 'Treatment is finished.' 🐆 Mina replies: 'No, maintenance begins.' Why is maintenance crucial?
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Periodontal maintenance is essential for long-term stability.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you've finally understood!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing a patient with periodontitis and significant stress, says: 'Stress can worsen the disease.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'No, it's a myth.' What is the impact of stress?
options: Stress increases inflammation and reduces immune response
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Chronic stress modifies the inflammatory response.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will take it into account in my treatments.'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami and 🐆 Mina discuss the future of periodontology. Sami says: 'Biomaterials will revolutionize regeneration!' Mina replies: 'The human factor remains key.' What is the future of regeneration?
options: Biomaterials and growth factors improve regeneration, but the clinician remains essential
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Advances in biomaterials are promising, but clinical expertise is irreplaceable.' 🦅 Sami: 'We keep our jobs!'
